name: Mumbai Metropolitan Region (provisional research extent)
description: An executed broad behavioural development baseline with mapped bus, suburban rail, metro and ferry services and a small representative-person population. No citywide scaling, calibration or complete all-mode coverage claim.

jurisdiction.statistical_agency: Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India
jurisdiction.transport_agency: Multiple operators and authorities; see source catalogue

boundary.dataset: Census of India 2011 district, taluka and village/ward boundaries (IIT Bombay MahaCensus shapefiles 1.1 and 1.2)

external_tier.reason: No external tier is modelled: through-demand from beyond the four 2011 census districts (the Pune, Nashik and Gujarat corridors) is not represented in the baseline. The four districts are the research OVERCOVERAGE the acquisition used, not the notified Mumbai Metropolitan Region: the 2011 Thane district includes today's Palghar, and the MMR takes only part of Thane, Palghar and Raigad. The MMR extent is the intended core once its villages are reconciled (decision D13, awaiting the user); this declaration names what the package actually holds.

mode_share_target.source: Census of India 2011 table B-28: other workers by mode of travel to place of work (residence-to-work only)
mode_share_target.geography: the four 2011 census districts Mumbai, Mumbai Suburban, Thane and Raigad, residence end
mode_share_target.note: The ONLY observed mode series the package holds is a 2011 commute-to-work table over 'other workers'; it is not an all-trip share and is fifteen years old. It is named here so the framework has a declared geography and series, not because it is fit to score the twelve modes: no mode target has been derived for this city, and mode_targets_by_mode.csv does not exist. The Greater Mumbai CMP executive summary (mumbai_cmp_summary) is acquired and not transcribed.
